scenario: A 26-year-old female presents after syncope with dizziness, vomiting, vague abdominal pain, pallor, and hypotension. The scenario focuses on recognition of ruptured ectopic pregnancy with intra-peritoneal bleeding, bedside ultrasound, massive transfusion, and urgent gynecology operative management.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: What brought you in today, and when did it start? Any pain or bleeding?

patient_emotion.notes: [clinician: What brought you in today, and when did it start? Any pain or bleeding?] This is a neutral intake question asking the patient to recount symptoms. No serious diagnosis, worsening news, or escalation is disclosed, so fear stays absent. No loss is named, so sadness stays absent. It is a single, simple question with no information overload, so overwhelm stays absent. The question is nonjudgmental with no blame or exposure, so shame stays absent.

messages.speaker: patient
messages.content: I passed out — just fainted. I've been really dizzy and weak, and I've been throwing up. My stomach hurts, kind of all over but nothing sharp. I feel really pale too. Can you just figure out what's wrong with me?

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Let's get a liter of normal saline in wide open now — she's hypotensive at 87/58 and looks like she's in shock.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Hanging 1 liter normal saline bolus now.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Get me a urine beta-hCG now — she's still borderline at 94/62 with abdominal pain, and I'm worried about a ruptured ectopic.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: I need one thing from you right now: when was your last period, and have you had any vaginal bleeding or spotting since?

patient_emotion.notes: [clinician: I need one thing from you right now: when was your last period, and have you had any vaginal bleeding or spotting since?] fear absent->present: the urgent focused question, combined with the preceding shock/ectopic concern context, signals a serious situation requiring immediate answers, which conveys threat and raises fear from absent to present. sadness stays absent: no loss or devastating outcome is named to the patient. overwhelm stays absent: this is a single, simple, focused question ('one thing'), which reduces rather than increases processing burden. shame stays absent: the question is neutral and nonjudgmental, no blame or exposure implied.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Urine beta-hCG is back — positive. Latest vitals: BP 89/59, HR 106, sats 98% on room air.

messages.speaker: patient
messages.content: I honestly can't remember exactly when my last period was — I'm not sure. And no, I haven't had any bleeding or spotting. Why does that matter? Just tell me what's going on.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Here's what's going on: your pregnancy test came back positive, your blood pressure is low at 89/59, and you fainted. That combination makes me worried about internal bleeding from a pregnancy growing outside the womb. I'm doing a quick ultrasound at the bedside right now to look for blood in your belly.
